🎵 Making the Chorus Pop: My Mixing Challenge! 🎧 . Struggling to achieve that epic transition from verse to chorus? 🎶 This artist wanted the change to be BIG, but the track was already pretty massive leading into the chorus. 🎵 So, I set myself a challenge: How can I make that transition without simply turning things down? . 💡 There are countless ways to make a song go big for the chorus, like changing treatments between verses and choruses – a classic move. But I decided to take it a step further. As we head towards the chorus, the track gradually collapses into mono. 🌀 . This technique has worked really well in creating a seamless transition. It goes to show that you don't always have to crank up the volume to make an impact. By going narrow and then wide again, we've achieved the desired impact without sacrificing any elements beforehand. 🎯 . . . #MixingMagic #ChorusTransition #MusicProduction101 #studionyne #mixing #mono #stereo

I spent hours recording a one minute mantra track to post here, recorded using advanced technology in full stereo. Then I decided to simply bounce it into mono lol 😂  I love mono mixes. You can get all perfectionist with panning , editing and effects but try and make it sound good in mono. Simple , the one sound . No frills or fuss just one channel to get right. For any of you young musicians out there - try your hand with one track. Black and white, the contrast deep, A frozen figure, lost in sleep. Chisel's kiss and hammer's bite, Captured in the soft twilight. Every groove and every line, A whisper from another time. In grayscale hues, it seems to sigh, A silent breath, a muted cry. Light and dark in dance entwined, A story told, yet undefined. Its features speak of joy and pain, Echoes of a sculptor’s strain. In every shade, a mystery, A silent witness to history. Photograph in monochrome, Turns the stone to flesh and bone. Timeless beauty, still, serene, A captured moment, ever keen. Through the lens, the past remains, In black and white, the essence gains.
